buckets.label: Must stay identical
buckets.hint: structural, and it will be compared across teams

buckets.label: Should vary locally
buckets.hint: The manager knows this and you don't

buckets.label: Not in the kit at all
buckets.hint: Needs judgment the manager isn't equipped to make

tasks.text: The date the new structure takes effect
tasks.reasoning: A hard fact that every affected employee will hear from a different manager and then compare. There is no version of local judgement that improves a date, and a discrepancy between two teams reads as either incompetence or concealment. Mark it fixed in the kit and say why.

tasks.text: Which roles are affected, and which aren't
tasks.reasoning: The single most compared statement in any change communication, and the one where a manager softening the edges to spare their team creates a real problem, an employee told 'probably fine' by their manager and 'in scope' by the letter has been failed by the kit, not the manager.

tasks.text: Which of this manager's people are directly affected, and how
tasks.reasoning: The most valuable thing in the kit and the thing that was impossible to produce at scale. It varies by definition. That's what makes it local rather than fixed. Note the distinction from item 2: the *rule* about who is in scope is fixed; the *application* to this team is what the local version supplies.

tasks.text: The severance terms an individual employee will be offered
tasks.reasoning: Individual employment consequences, with legal and contractual force, varying by tenure and jurisdiction. Every one of these that lands in a talking-points document becomes four hundred improvised answers to a question with exactly one correct answer. Put in the kit who to call, and when.

tasks.text: The order to cover things in, and what to address first
tasks.reasoning: Pure local judgement. A manager who knows their team opened last year's reorg with the wrong thing knows what to lead with this time. A kit that constrains ordering produces the read-aloud failure: the manager sounds like they are reciting, and the team is correct to notice.

tasks.text: The commitment that no one will be asked to relocate
tasks.reasoning: A promise. It will be quoted back, possibly years later, and possibly in a dispute. This is the category where AI-enabled local variation is most dangerous: four hundred slightly warmer restatements of a commitment is how an organization acquires obligations it never made.

tasks.text: Examples of how the change plays out in this team's day-to-day work
tasks.reasoning: The thing that makes the message concrete, and the thing the central team can't write. This is where AI's contribution is largest and safest, given structured inputs about the team, generating plausible local examples for the manager to check and correct is close to free, and the manager's correction is where the value is.

tasks.text: Whether a specific employee's visa status is affected by the site change
tasks.reasoning: Individual, legal, and consequential. A manager guessing here can cause serious harm to one person, and the kindest version of the kit removes the temptation entirely, not by warning the manager off it, but by naming the person who answers it, so the manager has somewhere to send it in the moment.

tasks.text: The two things most likely to land badly with this particular team
tasks.reasoning: The central team often knows this and never writes it down, because writing it down for four hundred managers meant writing four hundred different things. It is the highest-value local element in the kit and the clearest illustration of what changed: this was withheld by arithmetic, not by judgement.

tasks.text: The number of roles being reduced across the organization
tasks.reasoning: A number, and one employees will assemble from across teams whether or not you give it to them. Withholding it doesn't prevent the count; it just guarantees the count that circulates is wrong. Fixed, stated once, identically, and if the organization won't say it, that is a Decide-link conversation from Module 2, not a kit problem.
